name: MonarchConsentHistory
title: ConsentHistory
wrapsNative: VStack of bordered records with Text, Date.FormatStyle, Date.RelativeFormatStyle in a TimelineView(.everyMinute), MonarchEmptyState and MonarchButton
summary: A person's recorded consent decisions, newest first: when, how, which policy version and rules applied, and each category allowed or not.
whenToUse: On a privacy screen where people see what they agreed to, or in an admin view of one person's consent.
whenNotToUse: To ask for consent or change it, use the consent preferences sheet. For app tracking across other companies' apps, iOS requires the AppTrackingTransparency prompt instead.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, records: [MonarchConsentRecord], categories: [MonarchConsentCategory] = [], description: String? = nil, dateFormat: Date.FormatStyle = Date.FormatStyle(date: .abbreviated, time: .shortened), showsRelativeTime: Bool = false, exportTitle: String? = nil, labels: MonarchConsentHistoryLabels = MonarchConsentHistoryLabels(), onExport: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchConsentRecord { init(id: String, date: Date, method: MonarchConsentMethod, policyVersion: String, regime: MonarchConsentRegime, categories: [String: Bool], isGlobalPrivacyControl: Bool = false) }
enum MonarchConsentMethod: String { case acceptAll, rejectAll, custom, globalPrivacyControl, acknowledged, withdrawn }
enum MonarchConsentRegime: String { case optIn, optOut, notice }
struct MonarchConsentCategory { init(id: String, label: String) }

struct MonarchConsentHistoryLabels { init(method:, regime:, methodTitle:, policyVersionTitle:, regimeTitle:, categoriesTitle:, allowed:, denied:, signalPresent:, emptyTitle:, emptyMessage:, exportFailed:) }

options.name: records
options.description: The decisions, in any order; shown newest first.

options.name: categories
options.description: The product's categories, for their names and order. Ids in a record that are not listed are shown as the raw id, after the listed ones, sorted.

options.name: dateFormat
options.description: The format of each decision's date, in the current locale and time zone unless the style sets them.

options.name: showsRelativeTime
options.description: Also shows how long ago each decision was ("3 days ago"), updated every minute.

options.name: exportTitle
options.description: The title of the download button; name the format. "Download history" when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: methods, regimes, line names, Allowed and Not allowed, the signal line, the empty state and the export failure.

options.name: onExport
options.description: Builds and shares the file (for example with ShareLink or a document exporter). The button shows while there are records and is busy while this runs; throwing shows the failure.

states.name: records
states.description: One bordered record per decision on the surface colour.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState with a shield symbol, and no download button.

states.name: exporting
states.description: The download button shows its spinner and ignores further taps.

states.name: export failed
states.description: An icon and "The download did not start. Try again." in the strong danger colour under the header, announced; the button can be used again.

appearance: Records use the surface colour, a subtle border and 12-point corners. Dates use the strong body style; line names the caption style in the muted colour; values the body style. Allowed categories have a filled check in the strong success colour, refused ones an empty cross in the muted colour, each followed by the words. All are theme roles.
platformNotes: The web shows a table on wide containers and stacked cards below 640 points; iOS always shows the stacked records, which suit a phone and large text. The web's ConsentRecord stores the date as an ISO string; on iOS it is a Date. The web's locale and timeZone props are replaced by dateFormat; now is not needed because relative times come from the system clock. headingLevel has no iOS equivalent (the title is a header). The record types are defined here because the consent manager is not built on iOS; a later consent preferences sheet should use them. Android builds the same component. The parity map lists badge as a dependency; the method is plain text, as on the web, so no badge is used.
accessibility: The title and each decision's date have the header trait, so the headings rotor moves between decisions.
Each line is one element read as its name, value and any note ("Choice, Custom choice, Browser privacy signal present").
Each category is one element read as its name and "Allowed" or "Not allowed"; the label is built by a tested pure function and the icon and colour are not the only signal.
The download button is a MonarchButton with a 44-point touch target and a busy state while exporting.
The export failure is posted as an announcement.
edgeCases: Records with the same date keep the order they were given in.
A record with no categories shows no categories list.
The relative time is static text refreshed every minute, not a ticking clock.
Long policy versions and category names wrap.

examples.template:
MonarchConsentHistory(
    {{title}},
    records: records,
    categories: [
        MonarchConsentCategory(id: {{categories.0.id}}, label: {{categories.0.label}}),
        MonarchConsentCategory(id: {{categories.1.id}}, label: {{categories.1.label}}),
        MonarchConsentCategory(id: {{categories.2.id}}, label: {{categories.2.label}}),
        MonarchConsentCategory(id: {{categories.3.id}}, label: {{categories.3.label}}),
    ],
    description: {{description}}
)
.environment(\.locale, Locale(identifier: {{locale}}))
.environment(\.timeZone, TimeZone(identifier: {{timeZone}}) ?? .gmt)
